stack.title: Cyrus the Great
stack.hook: He conquered much of the known world, then became famous for allowing conquered peoples to return home and restore their religions. His name was Cyrus the Great, the only foreign ruler explicitly called God’s “anointed,” or messiah, in the Hebrew Bible.

cards.head: He conquered much of the known world, then became famous for allowing conquered peoples to return home and restore their religions.
cards.body: His name was Cyrus the Great, the only foreign ruler explicitly called God’s “anointed,” or messiah, in the Hebrew Bible.

cards.head: HE BUILT THE LARGEST EMPIRE THE WORLD HAD SEEN
cards.body: Cyrus founded the Persian Achaemenid Empire in the 6th century BCE. By the end of his reign, his empire stretched from Central Asia and the Indus region toward the Mediterranean.

cards.head: THEN HE CONQUERED BABYLON
cards.body: In 539 BCE, Cyrus captured Babylon, one of the greatest cities of the ancient world. Babylonian sources portray the takeover as remarkably orderly compared with the destruction often associated with ancient conquest.

cr.line: Persepolis Relief Priests.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: HE LET CONQUERED PEOPLES WORSHIP THEIR OWN GODS
cards.body: Rather than forcing one religion across his empire, Cyrus generally worked with local religious institutions and traditions. The famous Cyrus Cylinder describes him restoring sanctuaries and returning displaced divine images and peoples to their homes.

cards.head: THAT INCLUDED THE JEWS
cards.body: The Hebrew Bible says Cyrus allowed Jewish exiles in Babylon to return to Jerusalem and rebuild their Temple. Their ancestors had been deported after Babylon destroyed Jerusalem decades earlier.

cr.line: CyrustheGreatTomb 22059.jpg. Photo: Truth Seeker, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THE BIBLE GIVES HIM AN EXTRAORDINARY TITLE
cards.body: Isaiah 45 calls Cyrus God’s “anointed,” translated from the Hebrew mashiach, the word from which we get “messiah.” What makes this remarkable is that Cyrus wasn’t an Israelite king at all. He was a Persian ruler who worshipped other gods.

cards.head: HIS LEGACY SURVIVED FOR THOUSANDS OF YEARS
cards.body: Cyrus became remembered as an unusually effective ruler who governed a vast multicultural empire through a mixture of military power and accommodation.

cards.head: More than two thousand years later, he remains revered in Iranian history and appears in the Bible as the foreign king chosen to help restore Jerusalem.

cards.head: WHY A PERSIAN KING IS IN THE BIBLE
cards.body: Cyrus is the outsider the text calls anointed. Every argument about whether God works through people outside the faith comes back to him, which is why he keeps being cited by both sides.
